newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama transvestites seek their own red light zone.
newsitem.headline: Panama transvestites seek their own red light zone.

text.p: A group of transvestites asked on Wednesday for relief from what they called police harassment and a designated area where they can work as prostitutes.
Calling themselves the Third Sex Group, about 70 men petitioned Panama City officials to stop the police and establish a "red light zone" allowing them to work legally as prostitutes.
"Red light zones operate all over the world. What we want is one here," said the group's vice president Franklin Campbell, who prefers to be called Jazmine.
"The police harass us daily, beat us and rob us. We want an area where we can work and not be harassed," he said.
Prostitution between men and women is legal in Panama but homosexual activity is illegal.
"Moving homosexuals to a red zone is a reality we have to face," Mayor Mayin Correa said. "It's better to have them in one area than sprouting up all over the city under a storm of complaints."
City officials said they would respond to the petition next month. In the meantime, the transvestites agreed to limit their trade to late-night hours and undergo frequent medical checks.
